per_question.answer: The CAS number of Acetone is 67-64-1. *(acetone_sds.pdf – p. 1)*
The flash point of acetone is -17 °C, as stated on page 8 of the Safety Data Sheet according to Regulation (EC) No. 1907/2006 (REACH), amended by 2020/878/EU. *(acetone_sds.pdf – p. 8)*

The boiling point of acetone is 56.05°C, as stated in the Safety Data Sheet on page 8 *(acetone_sds.pdf – p. 8)*. However, another source mentions a boiling point of 78°C at 1.013 hPa *(acetone_sds.pdf – p. 9)*. This discrepancy might be due to different measurement conditions, such as pressure.
The lower and upper explosion limits (LEL and UEL) of acetone are 2.6 vol% (LEL) and 12.8 vol% (UEL) *(acetone_sds.pdf – p. 8)*.

The recommended glove material for handling acetone is Butyl caoutchouc (butyl rubber). The breakthrough time for this glove material, as specified in the provided Safety Data Sheet, is greater than 480 minutes (permeation: level 6) *(acetone_sds.pdf – p. 4)*.
The provided Safety Data Sheets indicate that the occupational exposure limit (TWA) for acetone is 1.210 mg/m³, which is equivalent to approximately 1210 ppm *(acetone_sds.pdf – p. 6)*.

After eye contact with acetone, the following first aid measures should be taken:

1. Irrigate copiously with clean, fresh water for at least 10 minutes, holding the eyelids apart. *(acetone_sds.pdf – p. 4)*
2. Consult an ophthalmologist if eye irritation persists. *(acetone_sds.pdf – p. 4)*
The recommended storage temperature for acetone is 15–25°C, as stated on page 8 of the Safety Data Sheet with article number 5025 *(Ireland (en) Page 8 / 20)*.
The provided Safety Data Sheets state that water jet is an unsuitable extinguishing media for an acetone fire. *(acetone_sds.pdf – p. 2, 8)*

The UN number for transporting acetone, according to the provided Safety Data Sheets, is UN1090 *(IMDG – Additional information – p. 13; REACH – Additional information – p. 1; ICAO-IATA/DGR – Additional information – p. 1)*.
